key_insight: This paper shows that multimodal LLMs can be made much faster by jointly adapting how many visual tokens they process and how much compute the language model uses. The key idea is to skip unnecessary work in both the input and the model, instead of optimizing only one side.
problem_solved: It addresses the high inference cost of multimodal large language models, which comes from processing many visual tokens and running expensive LLM computation. Existing methods often reduce only one dimension, leaving substantial inefficiency.
method: Jointly optimize visual token usage and LLM compute to reduce redundant processing.
Adaptively decide which visual tokens to keep or prune based on task relevance.
Adjust LLM computation dynamically, such as skipping unnecessary layers or heads during inference.
impact: This matters because it can make MLLMs more practical for real-world deployment by lowering latency and compute cost without sacrificing much performance. Practitioners can build faster, more efficient vision-language systems for edge devices and scalable production use.

paper_title: Look Less, Think Faster: Joint Token-Compute Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs
paper_authors: Pengcheng Wang, Zhiquan Wang, Jayoung Lee, Zhuoyan Xu, Ran Xu
